name: Electromagnetics: Poyntel
subtitle: Electromagnetics Fields Waves
shortDescription: Adaptive electromagnetics course in five cited 3D benches: touch sensor, coil, wireless charger, wave at glass, cable echo. Study aid only.
longDescription:
Electromagnetics: Poyntel teaches a first engineering electromagnetics course by letting you push on the physics. Each topic starts from a real device, and a 3D bench answers back while the numbers on screen are computed live.

FIVE BENCHES
Field Pad: a fingertip over a touchscreen sense cell. A potential surface, field lines and a Gauss-law flux check show why a finger steals charge from the electrode.
Coil Bench: a solenoid or a Helmholtz pair. Field lines close on themselves, and the axial plot comes from a numerical Biot-Savart sum over the wire.
Charger Pair: wireless charging. Slide the coils apart or off-centre and watch mutual inductance, emf and link efficiency change.
Wave Cell: a microwave-band plane wave meets a dielectric or conducting slab. E, B and the Poynting arrow are drawn with the correct sign and impedance scaling.
Echo Line: a voltage pulse runs down a cable, hits a mismatch and comes back. The echo ratio measured on the line is shown beside the reflection-coefficient formula.

LEARN YOUR WAY
Predict first, then test it on the bench. Choose how many questions you want (5, 10, 20, 40 or your own number) and a level from Beginner to Research. Practice shows a worked line after every answer. The mock exam uses numeric questions only, with an optional timer and no ads. A course path tracks fourteen topics, from Coulomb's law to transmission lines.

CHECKED AND CITED
Every numeric answer was recomputed by a second numerical method. Tap Sources on any screen to open the references (Cheng, Hayt, Griffiths, Sadiku, Ulaby, Pozar and MIT OpenCourseWare) in a window that returns you to the same place.

FREE WITH ADS
Short ads appear only at natural breaks and never during a mock exam. An optional monthly subscription (price shown by the App Store, 7-day free trial) removes them. Work stays on your device. No sign-in.
